::: {#sol-between-roots}

Let $x \in \set{x \in \reals : x^2 - 3x + 2 < 0}$.
Then $x$ is a real number, and $x^2 - 3x + 2 = (x - 1)(x - 2) < 0$.
We show that $1 < x < 2$, by ruling out the other two cases (@def-proof-by-cases).

- If $x \le 1$, then $x - 1 \le 0$ and $x - 2 < 0$,
  so $(x - 1)(x - 2) \ge 0$, since the product of two numbers that are not positive is not negative.
  That contradicts $(x - 1)(x - 2) < 0$.
- If $x \ge 2$, then $x - 1 > 0$ and $x - 2 \ge 0$,
  so $(x - 1)(x - 2) \ge 0$, again a contradiction.

So $1 < x < 2$, and so $0 < x < 3$.
So $x \in \set{x \in \reals : 0 < x < 3}$.

:::
